content.text: I'll create a channel beam (C-beam) that is 70mm wide, 40mm high, 450mm long with 5mm wall thickness, open on the top. Let me start by calculating the necessary dimensions for creating this shape.

input.PythonCode:
# Channel beam dimensions
width = 70  # mm
height = 40  # mm
length = 450  # mm
wall_thickness = 5  # mm

# For a channel beam open on top, we need:
# 1. Main block (full dimensions)
# 2. Subtract inner cavity

# Main block dimensions
main_block_x = length
main_block_y = width
main_block_z = height

# Inner cavity dimensions (to be subtracted)
# The cavity starts at wall_thickness from bottom and sides
cavity_x = length  # Full length
cavity_y = width - 2 * wall_thickness  # Width minus two side walls
cavity_z = height - wall_thickness  # Height minus bottom wall

# Cavity position (offset from origin)
cavity_x_pos = 0  # Same x position
cavity_y_pos = wall_thickness  # Offset by wall thickness from left
cavity_z_pos = wall_thickness  # Offset by wall thickness from bottom

print(f"Main block dimensions: {main_block_x} x {main_block_y} x {main_block_z}")
print(f"Cavity dimensions: {cavity_x} x {cavity_y} x {cavity_z}")
print(f"Cavity position: ({cavity_x_pos}, {cavity_y_pos}, {cavity_z_pos})")

1. A main block of 450mm × 70mm × 40mm
2. A subtracted cavity of 450mm × 60mm × 35mm, positioned 5mm from the left side and 5mm from the bottom
